title: Localization and Relative Quantification of Carbon Nanotubes in Cells with Multispectral Imaging Flow Cytometry
protocol: Disperse CNTs in cell culture water.
Sonicate the dispersion for 20 minutes in a bath-water sonicator at 20°C.
Grow human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) on 25 cm² plates in DMEM medium with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin streptomycin.
Prepare CNT solutions at concentrations of 0, 10, 20, and 50 µg/ml in complete medium.
Incubate cells with the CNT solutions at 37°C for 20 hours or at 4°C for 20 hours (2 ml of CNT suspension per 25 cm² plate).
Remove incubation medium after treatment.
Rinse cells with PBS.
Trypsinize and resuspend cells in complete DMEM medium.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 5 minutes at 1,200 rpm.
Replace the medium with paraformaldehyde 4% for 1 hour at 4°C.
Wash cells with PBS to preserve them.
Resuspend cells correctly in PBS to avoid aggregates during analysis and filter through a 50 μm mesh stainer.
Acquire images of cells using an ImageStream multispectral imaging flow cytometer.
Select an adapted magnification using a 40X objective.
Prepare a control sample without fluorochrome.
Prepare cells with a single-color positive control for each fluorochrome used.
Use the laser 488 nm to excite FITC and collect fluorescence emission through channel 02 (band-pass 480-560 nm).
Use channels 01 and 06 for bright field (BF) and dark field (DF), respectively.
Restrict analysis to the population of single cells using a biparametric dot plot representing 'aspect ratio' versus 'cell area'.
Discriminate single cells with standard area and aspect ratio close to 1 from multicellular events and debris.
Select cells in the focused plane using a biparametric dot plot plotting 'contrast' versus 'RMS gradient' on BF images.
Exclude unfocused cells showing both low rms gradient and low contrast in their BF images.
Determine the parameter which provides the best statistical separation between labeled and nonlabeled cells.
Use the mean pixel object feature as the most suitable parameter.
Trace an histogram using the mean pixel object parameter versus the normalized frequency to compare uptaken-CNTs for tested concentrations.
Trace a biparametric graph 'mean pixel object on BF' versus 'intensity on DF'.
Create a threshold mask that fits strongly absorbing dark spots on BF with a low intensity range of 0-533.
Conversely, create a mask fitting the pixels of high intensity in the DF ranging from 150-4095.
Plot a graph using the area of the mask to provide relative quantification of CNTs internalization at different concentrations.
Check the degree of correlation between two masks using a biparametric plot.
Create a mask fitting the interior of the cell by eroding M01 by 7 pixels.
Generate a mask for the membrane only using the Boolean equation: M01 and not Erode(M01, 7).
Create a mask to identify dark pixels on the membrane corresponding to CNTs with Intensity(M01 and not Erode(M01, 7), BF, 0-533).
Visualize different masks applied to a collection of cells to assess their relevance.
Apply the feature area on the mask selecting black pixels on the membrane 'Area_Intensity(M01 and not Erode(M01, 7), BF, 0-533)'.

Plot the black area on the membrane versus the black area on the entire cell (i.e., 'Area_ Intensity(M01 and not Erode(M01, 7), BF, 0-533' versus 'Area_ Intensity(M01, BF, 0-533)') to distinguish internalized CNTs from those adsorbed on the membrane.
